parts.problem_md:
In Uganda, the rate of inflation fell from 5% in 2014 to 2% in 2015.

Which conclusion can be drawn from this information?
parts.solution_md:
- **A is the correct answer** as even though inflation went from 5% to 2% - it was 2% on top of the 5% so prices were still rising (this is called disinflation)

  - B is incorrect as the cost of living rose by another 2%
  - C is incorrect as the impact on the standard of living cannot be calculated from this data
  - D is incorrect as Ugandan citizens were 2% worse off in 2015 than 2014

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Prices were higher in 2015 than in 2014.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: The cost of living fell between 2014 and 2015.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: The standard of living fell between 2014 and 2015.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Ugandan citizens were better off in 2015 than 2014.

parts.problem_md: What might cause prices to rise because of cost-push inflation?
parts.solution_md:
- **D is the correct answer** as wages/salaries are a cost of production and when they increase across an economy, it may lead to cost push inflation

  - A is incorrect as increased government spending is more likely to lead to demand pull inflation
  - B is incorrect as an increase in household consumption will lead to demand pull inflation
  - C is incorrect as a stronger balance of payments indicates exports are increasing - which will lead to demand pull inflation

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: an increase in government spending on education

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: an increase in household consumption

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: an increase in the balance of payments surplus

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: an increase in wages and salaries

parts.problem_md:
In January 2016 the rate of inflation in a country changed from 3% to 2%. In March 2016 the rate of inflation was 4%. What happened to the price level in January and March? | | January | March | |---|---|---| | A

B

C

D | fell

fell

rose

rose | fell

rose

fell

rose |
parts.solution_md:
- **D is the correct answer** as even though inflation went from 3% to 2% - it was 2% on top of the 3% so prices were still rising (this is called disinflation)

  - A is incorrect as price levels were still rising in January (2% on top of the previous 3%)
  - B is incorrect as price levels were still rising in January (2% on top of the previous 3%)

parts.problem_md:
The graph shows the rate of inflation in a country between 2000 and 2014.

![nov-2019v3qp-p1-cie-eco-q23](assets/001-nov-2019v3qp-p1-cie-eco-q23.png)

What can be concluded about average prices?
parts.solution_md:
- **C is the correct answer **the CPI value was higher each year (positive values) - although at a decreasing rate which is known as disinflation

  - A is incorrect as CPI does not fall in the period
  - B is incorrect as the average prices would have been at their highest level at the final year in the table - 2014/2015
  - D is incorrect as the CPI value is higher in 2014 than in 2010 - each year shows the growth in price levels on the previous year

parts.problem_md:
Four groups who are affected by changing economic conditions are creditors, debtors, exporters and importers.

Which pair is most likely to be disadvantaged by a high rate of inflation?
parts.solution_md:
- **A is correct **as creditors (anyone who borrowed money) are better off as the value of the money they owe - is worth less. Inflation also causes the price of exported goods to rise for people who are buying them from other countries - and rising prices lowers demand

  - B is incorrect as domestic inflation may mean consumers shop abroad and imports benefit
  - C is incorrect as debtors are worse off - we owe them money and the value of that money (what it can buy) has decreased
  - D is incorrect as debtors are worse off - we owe them money and the value of that money (what it can buy) has decreased

choices.text_md: creditors and exporters

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: creditors and importers

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: debtors and exporters

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: debtors and importers

parts.problem_md: An increase in which of the following is **least **likely to cause inflation?
parts.solution_md:
- **C is the correct answer **as an increase in income tax rates means consumers have less disposable income which will lower demand and possibly lower the inflation rate

  - A is incorrect as consumer spending increases demand and the inflation rate
  - C is incorrect as government spending increases demand and the inflation rate
  - D is incorrect as increased wages increases disposable income leading to increased demand and a rising inflation rate

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: government spending

choices.label: D

parts.problem_md: What is used to measure inflation?
parts.solution_md:
- **A is correct** as CPI is the measure of inflation

  - B is incorrect as the exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another
  - C is incorrect as GDP is the value of all output in an economy in a 1 year period
  - D is incorrect as an index of workers wages is not an index of the prices of goods/services

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: the consumer prices index (CPI)

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: the exchange rate

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: the gross domestic product (GDP)

choices.label: D

parts.problem_md:
A person receives annual interest of 4% on their savings. Inflation is 5% per annum.

What is the approximate change in the real value of their savings?
parts.solution_md:
- **B is the correct answer **as the inflation level (5%) is deducted from the savings rate (4%) to determine the real value of their savings (-1%)

  - A is incorrect as this calculation is just using the inflation rate
  - C is incorrect as this calculation ignores the inflation rate
  - D is incorrect as his calculation adds the savings rate and the inflation rate

parts.problem_md:
Some goods take a greater percentage of a typical household’s total spending than others.

How is this accounted for in the construction of a consumer prices index?
parts.solution_md:
- **B is the correct answer** as the weighting of a good represents the proportion of income usually spent on this good

  - A is incorrect as goods with higher expenditure are not deducted from the basket
  - C is incorrect as inflation as the CPI is calculated at a specific point in time - and then compared with the same time period in a previous year
  - D is incorrect as the price elasticity of demand does not mean that certain goods take a higher proportion of consumer's income - just that they are less willing to stop buying those products when prices increase

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: by deducting the goods

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: by giving a weight to the goods

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: by taking an average of price fluctuations during a year

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: by using the price elasticity of demand for the goods

parts.problem_md: What is **most **likely to cause a rise in the rate of inflation in an economy?
parts.solution_md:
- **C is the correct answer** as government spending is one component of demand and if it rises, then demand rises leading to an increase in the average price levels (inflation)

  - A is incorrect as cheaper imports will likely lead to more imports and less domestic demand. Less domestic demand will mean price levels fall (disinflation)
  - B is incorrect as falling wages will mean there is less disposable income which leads to less demand in the economy and falling prices (disinflation)
  - D is incorrect as increasing levels of unemployment will mean less income is spent in the economy, leading to a fall in demand, leading to falling price levels (disinflation)

choices.label: A

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: a fall in wage rates

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: a rise in the level of government spending

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: a rise in the level of unemployment

parts.problem_md:
In the construction of a consumer prices index (CPI), a total weight of 1000 is used.

If a weight of 300 is given to food and a weight of 150 is given to transport, then
parts.solution_md:
- **A is the correct answer** as the weighting shows what proportion of their income is spent on the good and 300 is double 150

  - B is incorrect as no information on other types of products are provided
  - C is incorrect as the index does not provide infromation on price changes, bur rather on the proportion of income spent on a particular category
  - D is incorrect as the weights may change on a regular basis

parts.problem_md: An economy is experiencing rising prices. Which government policy will help reduce consumer expenditure?
parts.solution_md:
- **A is the correct answer** as compulsory saving levels would mean that less money is spent by households on consumption, which would help to lower the rate of inflation

  - B is incorrect more investment in infrastructure increases demand leading to higher price levels (inflation)
  - C is incorrect as issuing more money causes inflation as consumers have more cash to spend in an economy
  - D is incorrect as reducing indirect taxes leaves consumers with more disposable income which can be spent - and when it is it may possibly add to inflation pressures

choices.label: B

choices.label: D

parts.problem_md:
Venezuela, a leading world oil producer, has experienced hyperinflation of over 400% per annum in recent years. How does hyperinflation affect an economy? | | prices | effect | |---|---|---| | **A**

**B**

**C**

**D** | fluctuate up and down

fluctuate up and down

rise very rapidly

rise very rapidly | consumers are uncertain about future price levels

consumers can anticipate future price levels

value of fixed assets remains stable

money has limited worth as a medium of exchange |
parts.solution_md:
- **D is the correct answer** as prices rise very rapidly under hyperinflation and money loses its value as a medium of exchange (which is why some countries switch from their currency to the US\$ when hyperinflation occurs)

  - A is incorrect as prices do not fluctuate down during hyperinflation
  - B is incorrect as prices do not fluctuate down during hyperinflation
  - C is incorrect as the value of fixed assets do not remain stable - their value fluctuates upwards too

parts.problem_md:

What is **most** likely to lead to an increase in demand-pull inflation?
parts.solution_md:
- **A is correct **as increased government spending is more likely to lead to demand pull inflation

  - B is incorrect as an increase in imports will likely lead to lower domestic demand and a possible fall in price levels
  - C is incorrect as higher income tax rates will lower disposable income leading to less demand and falling prices
  - D is incorrect as higher sales tax rates will lower disposable income leading to less demand and falling prices

parts.problem_md: What is included in the calculation of a consumer prices index (CPI)?
parts.solution_md:
- **A is the correct answer** the price of a basket of goods/services is the base measure used to calculate inflation

  - B is incorrect as inflation is not calculated using exports and imports
  - C is incorrect as the value of currency in international markets is measured using the exchange rate
  - D is incorrect as wages are not used to measure the CPI
